newsitem.title: UK: UK's Cambridge Antibody aims to float by end March.
newsitem.headline: UK's Cambridge Antibody aims to float by end March.

text.p: Cambridge Antibody Technology Group Plc said on Wednesday that it hoped to publish its flotation propectus before the end of February and to float on the stock exchange before the end of March.

Chief executive officer David Chiswell told Reuters in an interview, "One of our objectives was to lead the next round of biotech flotations this year and I think we are achieving that - we should be the first."

Chiswell said conditions in the sector were right for a flotation, which CAT hopes will raise between 30 million and 35 million stg, valuing the company at between 85 and 100 million stg. Positive sentiment towards the biotech sector, which has risen steadily in value since the start of the year, has helped CAT to move ahead quickly with its flotation, which was sheduled for the first half of 1997.
"The general sentiment of the sector has come right for us," said Chiswell, who founded CAT in 1990.

CAT, which specialises in using human monoclonal antibodies to discover and develop new drugs, has already tied up partnerships with a number of international drug companies including Pfizer Inc and Eli Lilly & Co. Last year it raised 10 million stg through a private placement.
